body.statement: Let Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser have a finite successful derivation that uses only contexts in \(H\) and supported denominators, and order its derivation DAG dependency-topologically with the published stable context and vertex order as tie-breaker. This derivation is used only as a comparison object. After \(k\) steps of the input-determined compiler, the emitted labelled kernels are algebraically equal after gate reinsertion to the first \(k\) published kernels, every registered denominator is the corresponding supported positive margin, and the compiler worklist is the canonically ordered unexecuted suffix of the same recursive tasks. Hence the fixed compiler cannot enter a residual failure state along a successful published recursion, and its accumulated terminal circuit is exactly the published identifying circuit.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the successful finite published derivation and its stated order, but do not supply it to the machine. We prove the three asserted invariants by induction on \(k\).

At \(k=0\), both constructions initialize every used context \(s\in H\) with
\[
 q_s(v)
 =p_H(V=v\mid S=s)
 =\frac{p_H(v,s)}{\sum_{v'}p_H(v',s)}.
\tag{6}
\]
The denominator is the same supported context mass in both constructions and is positive by (1). The task lists are the same initial recursive query in the same fixed context and vertex order.

Assume the invariant after \(k\) steps. Because corresponding kernels are equal and their graphs and labels coincide, every graphical predicate inspected by the compiler has the same truth value as in the next published recursive case. If an actual forced gate remains, both evaluate the same stored multiplexer occurrence, and gate reinsertion makes the rewritten normalized kernel equal to the published kernel. If no gate remains and the proper-ancestor or intervention-augmentation predicate holds, both compute the same unique vertex set and the same finite marginal. If the postintervention graph has several districts, both compute its unique district partition and create the same proper child tasks in stable order. In the one-district recursive case, both compute the same required district and the same proper ambient district. The compiler fixes only their prescribed complement and uses the common stable order among valid prefixes. Equations (2)--(3) show inductively that its quotient kernel and margin are the same as the corresponding published quotient and supported margin. Finally, an ambient-district terminal case appends the same topological factor and the same marginal.

Thus in every case the next emitted kernel agrees algebraically after gate reinsertion, the newly registered denominator is the same supported margin, and removing the executed task and inserting its canonically ordered children changes both worklists in the same way. This proves the invariant at \(k+1\). It also proves that the compiler's exact cross-multiplied local obligations hold, rather than inferring them merely from semantic equality.

If the fixed compiler reached the residual failure predicate before the published derivation ended successfully, the induction would give the same current task to the published recursion, and all preceding graphical predicates would fail there as well. That is the published failure case, contradicting successful termination. Hence no such diversion occurs. At the final index, all tasks are completed and their ordered sum--product composition is the published circuit. The accumulated circuit is inserted into the projection list, and the preceding algebraic identities give its verifier identity modulo \(\mathcal J\). The successful derivation is therefore simulated by the sole input-determined compiler; it was never installed as an agenda.
